title: Genesis 26 — Yitzchaq at Gerar, the wife-sister episode, the wells, and the covenant at Be'er Sheva

citations: Alter 1981 *Art of Biblical Narrative* ch. 3 on the type-scene
verdicts.reasoning: Famine-doublet language (*mi-l'vad ha-ra'av ha-rishon asher hayah bi-mei Avraham*) is rendered transparently; the cross-reference to Gen 12:10's *va-yhi ra'av ba-aretz* is appropriate. ASV-baseline phrasing.
*Al-tered Mitsraymah* (*do not go down to Mitsrayim*) is rendered directly; the Yitzchaq-specific prohibition framing is supported by Sarna's land-confinement reading.
*Gur ba-aretz ha-zot* / *eheyeh imkha* / land-and-oath promise — standard patriarchal-promise vocabulary; ASV-baseline accurate.
*K-kokhvei ha-shamayim* / seed-and-land / *hitbarakhu b-zar'akha kol goyei ha-aretz* — standard formulae; rendering matches Westermann and Sarna.

*Eqev asher shama Avraham b-qoli* / fourfold *mishmarti mitzvotai chuqotai v-torotai* preserved in ASV-baseline four-noun form so the source-critical anomaly remains visible to readers. The Sinaitic-retrojection framing in commentary is mainstream-critical-consensus.
*Va-yeshev Yitzchaq bi-Gerar* — single-clause; literal.
*Achoti hi* / *yare lemor ishti* / *tovat mar'eh* — the wife-sister verbal-cluster recycled from Gen 12 / Gen 20; ASV-baseline.

*M-tzacheq et Rivkah ishto* — the direct-object disambiguates conjugal sense, as confirmed by Sarna and Alter. *Sporting* retains the wordplay with Yitzchaq's name; modern explicit renderings (*fondling/caressing*) would sharpen the sense at the cost of the paronomasia. Defensible compromise.
*Hineh ishtekha hi / akh / pen-amut aleha* — standard recognition-and-explanation exchange; rendering matches the Gen 12 and Gen 20 parallels structurally.
*Mah-zot asita lanu* / *kim'at shakhav* / *asham* — guilt-language rendered conventionally. NJPS and NRSV concur.
*Ha-nogea ba-ish ha-zeh u-v-ishto mot yumat* — death-penalty edict; ASV-baseline accurate.
*Me'ah she'arim* rendered *a hundredfold* — the idealized-superabundant numeric idiom; Sarna's hinge-reading on the agricultural-prosperity / Philistine-envy pivot is well-supported.
*Va-yigdal ha-ish va-yelekh halokh v-gadel ad ki-gadal me'od* — the three-fold intensification rendered idiomatically; ASV phrasing preserves the progression.

*Miqneh-tzon u-miqneh baqar va-avudah rabbah* — Yitzchaq's compound pastoral-agricultural wealth correctly noted as distinct from Avraham's pure-pastoral wealth at Gen 13:2 and Ya'aqov's at Gen 30:43.
Wells-stopped-with-earth — verbal forms straightforward; rendering accurate.
*Lekh me-imanu ki-atzamta mimenu me'od* — expulsion-utterance; ASV-baseline.
*Va-yichan b-nachal Gerar* — *encamped in the wadi of Gerar*; *nachal* as *wadi* is the standard ANE-geographically-accurate rendering.
*Va-yashav Yitzchaq va-yachpor* / re-naming pattern — the paternal-continuation signature is editorially defensible per Westermann's reading of the Yitzchaq-cycle as Avraham-cycle-replayed.
*Be'er mayim chayyim* — *well of living water*; standard.
*Esek* (עֵשֶׂק) / *ki hit'as'qu imo* — etymology in-text; root *a-s-q* near-hapax. Rendering preserves both transliteration and etiology.
*Sitnah* (שִׂטְנָה) / *va-yarivu gam aleha* — root *s-t-n* connection to *ha-satan* correctly flagged-but-not-conflated per Sarna and Westermann.
*Rechovot* / *hirchiv YHWH lanu u-farinu va-aretz* — the *p-r-h* (fruitful) echo of Gen 1:28 / 9:1 / 17:6 / 35:11 correctly noted; three-fold progression *contention → opposition → room* coherent.
*Va-ya'al mi-sham Be'er Sheva* — *and he went up from there to Be'er Sheva*; literal.

citations: Nissinen 2003 *Prophets and Prophecy in the ANE* (SBL WAW 12)
verdicts.reasoning: Four-formula compound theophany rendered transparently. *Anokhi Elohei Avraham avikha* preserves *Elohim* in transliteration per glossary; *al-tira ki-itkha anokhi* / blessing-multiplication / Avraham-merit grounds-clause all directly from MT. The Alt 1929 ancestral-god framing in commentary is mainstream-critical with appropriate refinement notes.
*Va-yiven sham mizbeach va-yiqra b-shem YHWH* / pitching tent / well-digging — the patriarchal-altar formula recurrence; paternal-continuation reading is sound.

Avimelekh + Achuzzat + Phicol delegation — the doublet relationship to Gen 21:22-32 is correctly noted; the Pichol name-recurrence across two nominally-distinct generations is editorially-flagged-not-resolved.
*Maduua batem elai v-atem snetem oti* — the grievance-question; rendering accurate.

*Ra'o ra'inu ki-hayah YHWH imakh* — the YHWH/Elohim divine-name shift from Gen 21:22 (Elohim) to Gen 26:28 (YHWH) is correctly flagged as a possible J/E documentary-source signal per Westermann and Friedman.
*Im-ta'aseh imanu ra'ah / nashlachakha b-shalom / atah atah barukh YHWH* — covenant-stipulation language; rendering accurate.
*Va-ya'as lahem mishteh va-yokhlu va-yishtu* — feast-meal; literal.
*Va-yashkimu va-yishav'u ish l-achiv* — niphal-reciprocal swearing; the *yishav'u* verb-form is the key for the v 33 Be'er Sheva etymology.
*Matza'nu mayim* — water-discovery announcement; literal.

*Shiv'ah* (the oath-sense alone) — single-sense doublet of the layered Gen 21:31 double-etymology. The partial-vs-layered framing is supported by the wider doublet pattern; appliesTo expansion of `be-er-sheva-folk-etymology` is correct.

Esav at 40 / two Chitti wives (Yehudit bat-Be'eri, Basemat bat-Elon) — wife-list rendered transparently. The wife-list inconsistency across Gen 26:34 / 28:9 / 36:2-3 is correctly flagged in commentary with both rabbinic-harmonizing and modern-source-critical readings.
*Va-tihyeinah morat ruach l-Yitzchaq u-l-Rivkah* — the *morat ruach* construct (near-hapax) preserved in fixed-phrase rendering; the Gen 27 narrative-setup function is correctly identified.

glossaryReview.reasoning: The Sinaitic-retrojection / P-or-late-D layer reading is mainstream modern-critical-consensus and is properly cited. The four lexemes' Pentateuchal distributions (mishmeret as Priestly cultic-duty; mitzvot as Sinaitic-Mosaic commandments; chuqot as engraved-decree-statute; torot as the rare-plural teachings) are accurate to BDB / HALOT. The grounds-clause-structure parallel to Deut 7:8 / 9:5 is correctly identified. Rabbinic-traditional reading (m. Qidd. 4:14; b. Yoma 28b; Gen Rab 64:4; Rashi) flagged-not-preempted. claim_type=direct is defensible: the lexical-distributional facts are documentary and the source-critical reading is consensus, not synthesis.

The not-conflated treatment is the right call and the forward-reference for the future Job 1-2 / Zech 3 entries is helpful, not confusing.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִלְּבַד֙ הָרָעָ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בִּימֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יִצְחָ֛ק אֶל־אֲבִימֶּ֥לֶךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים גְּרָֽרָה׃

i18n.en: And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Avraham. And Yitzchaq went to Avimelekh king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter opens with the second of two patriarchal famine-narratives: *mi-l'vad ha-ra'av ha-rishon asher hayah bi-mei Avraham* — *besides the first famine that was in the days of Avraham* — explicitly cross-referencing Gen 12:10's *va-yhi ra'av ba-aretz* and signalling the chapter's doublet relationship to the Avram-in-Mitsrayim narrative of Gen 12 and the Avraham-Avimelekh-of-Gerar narrative of Gen 20. Gen 26 is the **third instance** of the wife-sister type-scene (see [wife-sister-type-scene](#wife-sister-type-scene); Alter *The Art of Biblical Narrative* 1981, ch. 3 is the canonical literary-critical treatment). The chapter does not introduce the type-scene; it closes it, replaying the inherited material with Yitzchaq and Rivkah in the patriarchal-couple roles and Avimelekh of Gerar in the foreign-king role (now structurally on his second appearance in the Genesis Avimelekh-cycle, after Gen 20-21).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־תֵּרֵ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה שְׁכֹ֣ן בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH appeared to him, and said, Do not go down to Mitsrayim; dwell in the land of which I shall tell you.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's first theophany — *va-yera elav YHWH* — is the editorial-pivot. The patriarchal-theophany formula (see [va-yera-yhwh-theophany](#va-yera-yhwh-theophany)) marks the moment Yitzchaq, unlike his father at Gen 12:10, is **explicitly forbidden to descend to Mitsrayim**: *al-tered Mitsraymah* — *do not go down to Mitsrayim*. The prohibition is editorially loaded. Gen 12:10's Avram had descended without prior divine instruction; Gen 20:1's Avraham had moved south to Gerar without divine instruction; only Yitzchaq receives the explicit YHWH-given travel directive. **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 183 reads the prohibition as Yitzchaq-specific: the Yitzchaq-cycle distinguishes the second patriarch from the first by his geographical-confinement to the promised land (he is the only patriarch who never leaves it). The wider editorial pattern is the *land-confinement* register: Yitzchaq is the patriarch whose entire narrative-cycle is contained within the borders of the land that the Avrahamic-covenant has promised. The implication for the wife-sister-type-scene replay is that the Yitzchaq-cycle's version is **structurally truncated**: Yitzchaq does not descend to a foreign-imperial-court (Egypt at Gen 12; Gerar of an earlier Avimelekh-court at Gen 20) but stays within Gerar's nearer-Philistine-pastoral context.

paragraphs.text: גּ֚וּר בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶֽהְיֶ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ וַאֲבָרְכֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־לְךָ֣ וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֗ אֶתֵּן֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָֽאֲרָצֹ֣ת הָאֵ֔ל וַהֲקִֽמֹתִי֙ אֶת־הַשְּׁבֻעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם אָבִֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you; for to you, and to your seed, I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Avraham your father.

paragraphs.text: וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֤י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְזַרְעֲךָ֔ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָאֲרָצֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑ל וְהִתְבָּרֲכ֣וּ בְזַרְעֲךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens, and will give to your seed all these lands; and in your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.

paragraphs.text: עֵ֕קֶב אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמַ֥ע אַבְרָהָ֖ם בְּקֹלִ֑י וַיִּשְׁמֹר֙ מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֔י מִצְוֺתַ֖י חֻקּוֹתַ֥י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי׃

i18n.en: Because Avraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The chapter's clearest source-critical signal.** The four nouns *mishmarti, mitzvotai, chuqotai, v-torotai* (*my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws*) name the four primary categories of Pentateuchal legal-stipulation vocabulary — all of which properly belong to the Sinaitic / Mosaic legal-corpus (Exodus 19 onward) — and apply them to Avraham, who in the surrounding narrative receives covenant promises (Gen 12:1-3; 15; 17) but no enumerated law-code. *Mishmeret* is a Priestly cultic-duty term (Lev 8:35; Num 1:53; 3:7-8; 18:3-5); *mitzvot* is the Pentateuch's primary term for Sinaitic commandments (Exod 16:28, 20:6; the entire Deuteronomic *passim*-distribution); *chuqot* is the engraved-decree-law term, concentrated in the P and D strata; *torot* (plural — a comparatively rare form, 10 HB occurrences) names multiple distinct legal *teachings*. The four-noun cluster as a unit recurs only in late-Deuteronomistic and post-exilic contexts — Deut 11:1; 26:17; 28:1; 1 Kgs 2:3; 8:58; 9:6; 2 Kgs 17:13; 23:3; Mal 3:22 — making the Gen 26:5 application editorially anomalous.

**Modern critical reading.** Wellhausen *Prolegomena* 1885, Skinner *ICC Genesis* 1910 pp. 363-364, von Rad *Genesis* 1956 OTL, Westermann *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 425-426, Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 184-185, Wenham *WBC* 1994 pp. 189-190, Hamilton *NICOT* 1995 pp. 195-196, Alter 2004 p. 134, and Friedman *Who Wrote the Bible?* 1987 all read the verse as a late-Deuteronomistic or Priestly editorial gloss — a Sinaitic-retrojection imposing the Mosaic-legal vocabulary on the patriarchal narrative. The rabbinic-traditional alternative (m. Qidd. 4:14; b. Yoma 28b; Gen Rab 64:4; Rashi at Gen 26:5) harmonizes by holding that Avraham observed the entire Torah by anticipation. Both readings are documented in [mishmeret-mitzvot-chuqim-torot-fourfold-covenant](#mishmeret-mitzvot-chuqim-torot-fourfold-covenant); the WoH translation preserves the ASV-baseline four-noun rendering so that the source-critical anomaly is visible to the reader.

**Structural function.** The verse caps the YHWH-self-disclosure to Yitzchaq at vv 2-5 by providing the *grounds* for the promise-reissue: Yitzchaq receives the promise *eqev asher shama Avraham b-qoli* — *because Avraham obeyed my voice*. The grounds-clause-structure (gift-grounded-in-the-fathers'-merit) is a Deuteronomic signature, structurally parallel to Deut 7:8 and 9:5, reinforcing the late-stratum-attribution.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִצְחָ֖ק בִּגְרָֽר׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq dwelt in Gerar.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּשְׁאֲל֞וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ לְאִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא כִּ֤י יָרֵא֙ לֵאמֹ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֔י פֶּן־יַֽהַרְגֻ֜נִי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ עַל־רִבְקָ֔ה כִּֽי־טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה הִֽיא׃

i18n.en: And the men of the place asked him about his wife; and he said, She is my sister; for he feared to say, My wife; lest, said he, the men of the place should kill me on account of Rivkah, because she was a woman beautiful of appearance.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּ֣י אָֽרְכוּ־ל֥וֹ שָׁם֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף אֲבִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים בְּעַ֖ד הַֽחַלּ֑וֹן וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה יִצְחָק֙ מְצַחֵ֔ק אֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Avimelekh king of the Philistines looked out through the window, and saw, and behold, Yitzchaq was sporting with Rivkah his wife.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Va-yar v-hineh Yitzchaq m-tzacheq et Rivkah ishto* — the piel participle *m-tzacheq* (from *tz-ch-q*, the root behind Yitzchaq's own name) here names **conjugal-intimate play** between husband and wife, visible enough through the window for Avimelekh to recognize the marriage. The conjugal sense is determined by the verse's grammatical and contextual disambiguators: (i) the explicit direct object *et Rivkah ishto* names the wife; (ii) the verb is observed through a window — a culturally-marked sight-line for intimate behavior; (iii) the observation is sufficient to disclose the marriage to Avimelekh, who immediately concludes *hineh ishtekha hi* (v 9). Mere *playing* would not have been disclosive. **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 185, **Alter** 2004 p. 134, **Westermann** 1985 p. 425, and the modern English versions (NJPS / NRSV / NIV-2011 *fondling, caressing*) all read the conjugal sense as determinative.

The same piel participle was used contestedly at Gen 21:9 (Sarah saw Yishma'el *m-tzacheq* — see [metzacheq-ishmael-debate](#metzacheq-ishmael-debate) for the four-reading dispute). The two attestations are not in competition: Gen 26:8 is grammatically-determinate (the direct object disambiguates); Gen 21:9 is grammatically-indeterminate (no direct object in MT). The piel of *tz-ch-q* is deliberately polysemous across the corpus — playful-laughter (Gen 21:6); mocking-joking (Gen 19:14); erotic-love-play (Gen 26:8; Gen 39:14-17); ritual-cultic revelry (Exod 32:6); performance-spectacle (Judg 16:25) — and each attestation is disambiguated by context. See [metzacheq-conjugal-vs-contested-disambiguation](#metzacheq-conjugal-vs-contested-disambiguation) for the full polysemy treatment.

The Hebrew also activates the **paronomastic name-play**: *Yitzchaq m-tzacheq* — *Yitzchaq Yitzchaq-ing* / *the-laugher laughing-erotically*. The verb-name homophony continues the Gen 17-21 laughter-and-name-play arc (see [yitzchaq-name-etymology-laughter-pattern](#yitzchaq-name-etymology-laughter-pattern)). The WoH translation preserves the ASV-baseline *sporting* — a euphemistic-archaic register that preserves the conjugal sense while keeping the wordplay-with-the-name active. Modern explicit renderings (*fondling*, *caressing*) sharpen the conjugal sense at the cost of obscuring the name-play.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְיִצְחָ֗ק וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַ֣ךְ הִנֵּ֤ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֙ הִ֔וא וְאֵ֥יךְ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יִצְחָ֔ק כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן־אָמ֖וּת עָלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And Avimelekh called Yitzchaq, and said, Behold, of a surety she is your wife; and how did you say, She is my sister? And Yitzchaq said to him, Because I said, Lest I die because of her.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ מַה־זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֑נוּ כִּ֠מְעַט שָׁכַ֞ב אַחַ֤ד הָעָם֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתֶּ֔ךָ וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ עָלֵ֖ינוּ אָשָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And Avimelekh said, What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֣ו אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הַנֹּגֵ֜עַ בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה וּבְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

i18n.en: And Avimelekh commanded all the people, saying, He that touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּזְרַ֤ע יִצְחָק֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔וא וַיִּמְצָ֛א בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַהִ֖וא מֵאָ֣ה שְׁעָרִ֑ים וַֽיְבָרֲכֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq sowed in that land, and found in the same year a hundredfold; and YHWH blessed him.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yizra Yitzchaq ba-aretz ha-hi va-yimtza ba-shanah ha-hi me'ah she'arim* — *Yitzchaq sowed in that land, and found in the same year a hundredfold*. The verse is one of the patriarchal-narratives' only explicit **agricultural-farming** notices: Yitzchaq is depicted as a sedentary grain-farmer rather than as a pastoral-nomadic herder. The hundredfold-yield (*me'ah she'arim*) is an idealized-superabundant number; the in-land famine of v 1 has been reversed by divine-blessing. **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 184 reads the verse as the chapter's hinge between the wife-sister narrative (vv 1-11) and the Philistine-envy / well-conflict narrative (vv 12-22): Yitzchaq's prosperity is the cause of the Philistines' envy at v 14, and the well-stopping (v 15) and the Avimelekh-expulsion (v 16) are the consequence. The pastoral-and-agricultural compound character of Yitzchaq's wealth (*miqneh-tzon u-miqneh baqar v-avudah rabbah* at v 14 — *flocks, herds, and a great household / cultivated land*) is distinct from Avraham's pure-pastoral wealth (Gen 13:2) and Ya'aqov's later pure-pastoral wealth (Gen 30:43); Yitzchaq is the *settled* patriarch.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְגָדֵ֔ל עַ֥ד כִּֽי־גָדַ֖ל מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: And the man grew great, and went on growing greater, until he became very great.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ מִקְנֵה־צֹאן֙ וּמִקְנֵ֣ה בָקָ֔ר וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֑ה וַיְקַנְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And he had possessions of flocks, and possessions of herds, and a great household; and the Philistines envied him.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yqan'u oto Pelishtim* — *and the Philistines envied him*. The verse marks the **structural-pivot** to the well-conflict narrative. The Philistine envy is the chapter's depiction of inter-ethnic economic-territorial competition: Yitzchaq's prosperity in their land creates the political-economic tension that produces both the well-stopping (v 15) and the Avimelekh-expulsion (v 16). The pattern is a recurring HB type-scene: prosperity-of-the-resident-alien-provokes-host-population-envy (cf. Exod 1:7-10, the Pharaoh's response to Israelite multiplication in Mitsrayim; **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* p. 184 notes the cross-cycle parallel — the Yitzchaq-in-Gerar story prefigures the Israel-in-Mitsrayim story in compressed-narrative form).

paragraphs.text: וְכָל־הַבְּאֵרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו בִּימֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יו סִתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְמַלְא֖וּם עָפָֽר׃

i18n.en: Now all the wells which his father's servants had dug in the days of Avraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִצְחָ֑ק לֵ֚ךְ מֵֽעִמָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי־עָצַֽמְתָּ־מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: And Avimelekh said to Yitzchaq, Go from us, for you are much mightier than we.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם יִצְחָ֑ק וַיִּ֥חַן בְּנַֽחַל־גְּרָ֖ר וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq departed from there, and encamped in the wadi of Gerar, and dwelt there.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יִצְחָ֜ק וַיַּחְפֹּ֣ר ׀ אֶת־בְּאֵרֹ֣ת הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ בִּימֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יו וַיְסַתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֣וֹת אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶן֙ שֵׁמ֔וֹת כַּשֵּׁמֹ֕ת אֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ן אָבִֽיו׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq dug again the wells of water, which they had dug in the days of Avraham his father; for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Avraham. And he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yiqra la-hen shemot ka-shemot asher qara la-hen aviv* — *and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them*. The verse is an editorial-keystone for the Yitzchaq-cycle's **continuity-with-Avraham character**. Yitzchaq's distinctive narrative-feature across the chapter is **paternal-continuation** rather than independent innovation: he digs his father's wells, names them by his father's names, receives the same theophany-formulae (*va-yera elav YHWH*; the *al-tira ki-itkha anokhi*; the *anokhi Elohei Avraham avikha*), the same land-and-seed promises (vv 3-4), and the same Avimelekh-treaty (vv 26-31). The Yitzchaq-cycle is structurally the **Avraham-cycle replayed** — a deliberate editorial choice that places Yitzchaq as the patriarch of *covenant-transmission* rather than *covenant-initiation*. **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 423-424 reads the Yitzchaq-cycle's structural-truncation as editorial: the second patriarch is depicted not as a new patriarch but as the **first heir** — the one who receives, preserves, and transmits the Avrahamic-covenant without modification.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּחְפְּר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־יִצְחָ֖ק בַּנָּ֑חַל וַיִּ֨מְצְאוּ־שָׁ֔ם בְּאֵ֖ר מַ֥יִם חַיִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq's servants dug in the wadi, and found there a well of living water.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּרִ֜יבוּ רֹעֵ֣י גְרָ֗ר עִם־רֹעֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק לֵאמֹ֖ר לָ֣נוּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵֽׁם־הַבְּאֵר֙ עֵ֔שֶׂק כִּ֥י הִֽתְעַשְּׂק֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the herdsmen of Gerar contended with Yitzchaq's herdsmen, saying, The water is ours. And he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.

paragraphs.commentary: **The first of three wells in the chapter's deliberate three-well place-name etymology triad — *Esek*, *Sitnah*, *Rechovot*.** The name *Esek* (עֵשֶׂק — *Contention*) derives from the verb *hit'as'qu* in the in-text etiology: *ki hit'as'qu imo* — *because they contended with him*. The root *a-s-q* (*contend, strive, dispute*) is a hapax-or-near-hapax HB verbal-root; the noun *Esek* itself is a hapax outside this place-name. The contention-register is **legal-economic** — water-rights litigation — rather than military. See [esek-sitnah-rechovot-well-name-triad](#esek-sitnah-rechovot-well-name-triad) for the triad's full structural treatment.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּחְפְּרוּ֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וַיָּרִ֖יבוּ גַּם־עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמָ֖הּ שִׂטְנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they dug another well, and they contended for that also; and he called its name Sitnah.

paragraphs.commentary: The second well — *Sitnah* (שִׂטְנָה — *Opposition / Hostility / Accusation*). The name derives from the **root *s-t-n*** — **the same root as *ha-satan*** (הַשָּׂטָן, *the adversary / the accuser*) at Job 1-2, Zech 3:1-2, and 1 Chr 21:1. The root's primary register is **hostile-opposition / adversarial-accusation**. The abstract-noun *sitnah* has a sparse HB distribution: Gen 26:21 (here) and Ezra 4:6 (the *sitnah al yoshvei Yehudah* — the *accusation* sent against the inhabitants of Yehudah under Achashverosh). **The root-connection to *ha-satan* is flagged but not conflated**: the place-name and the later adversarial-figure share the root, but inhabit distinct semantic registers — the place-name is in the *legal-or-territorial-contention* register; the *ha-satan* is in the *divine-council-prosecutor* register. **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 186 notes the root-connection without conflating; the WoH treatment follows. See [esek-sitnah-rechovot-well-name-triad](#esek-sitnah-rechovot-well-name-triad) for the cross-corpus distribution and the not-conflated treatment.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעְתֵּ֣ק מִשָּׁ֗ם וַיַּחְפֹּר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וְלֹ֥א רָב֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ רְחֹב֔וֹת וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־עַתָּ֞ה הִרְחִ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה לָ֖נוּ וּפָרִ֥ינוּ בָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And he removed from there, and dug another well; and they did not contend for it. And he called its name Rechovot; and he said, For now YHWH has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.

paragraphs.commentary: The third and resolving well — *Rechovot* (רְחֹבוֹת — *Broad-Places / Room*). The name derives from the root ***r-ch-v*** (*be wide, be broad, make-room*); the in-text etiology explicitly cites the verb *hirchiv* (hiphil — *made-room*): *ki-atah hirchiv YHWH lanu u-farinu va-aretz* — *for now YHWH has made-room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land*. The triad's structural progression — *contention → opposition → room and fruitfulness* — resolves at the third well, with the *u-farinu va-aretz* clause echoing the Gen 1:28 / 9:1 / 17:6 / 35:11 fruitfulness-formula. The pattern is a **three-fold-progression-with-resolution**: three iterations of conflict, the third yielding resolution. **Yitzchaq's distinctive character** as patriarch is editorially-encoded in the naming-pattern: he does not fight back at the wells; he moves on and digs another. **Sarna** p. 186: *the names memorialize the conflict; Yitzchaq's pastoral-pacifist response is editorially-foregrounded*.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

i18n.en: And he went up from there to Be'er Sheva.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֕י אֱלֹהֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יךָ אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֣ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבֵֽרַכְתִּ֙יךָ֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֔ בַּעֲב֖וּר אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And YHWH appeared to him the same night, and said, I am the Elohim of Avraham your father; do not fear, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your seed for my servant Avraham's sake.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The chapter's keystone theophany — and one of the densest divine-self-disclosure verses in the patriarchal narratives.** The verse compounds **four canonical formulae** into a single divine-speech: (i) the *va-yera elav YHWH* theophany-formula (see [va-yera-yhwh-theophany](#va-yera-yhwh-theophany)); (ii) the *anokhi Elohei Avraham avikha* ancestral-god self-disclosure formula; (iii) the *al-tira ki-itkha anokhi* fear-not divine-encouragement formula; (iv) the *u-verakhtikha v-hirbeiti et-zar'akha* blessing-and-multiplication formula. The Yitzchaq-cycle's editorial signature is its **formulaic density**: Yitzchaq, the least-narratively-developed of the three patriarchs, receives the most-densely-formulaic divine-encouragement.

**The *al-tira ki-itkha anokhi* formula** — *do not fear, for I am with you* — is the foundational HB divine-encouragement-opener. It is one of the most distributionally extensive recurring formulae in the canon, deployed at moments of theophany or prophetic-call (Gen 15:1; Exod 3:6; Isa 6, 41:10; Jer 1:8; Ezek 2-3; Dan 10), at moments of military or political crisis (Exod 14:13; Num 14:9, 21:34; Josh 8:1; 2 Kgs 6:16), and at moments of eschatological-restoration prophecy (Isa 41-44; Jer 30, 46; Zech 8; Hag 2). The ANE context is well-documented: **Conrad** 1985 *Fear Not Warrior* (Brown Judaic Studies 75) distinguishes the warrior-encouragement form (recurring in Mari-letters and Neo-Assyrian prophecy-collections like the *Esarhaddon-prophecies*) from the patriarchal-encouragement form. **Nissinen** 2003 *Prophets and Prophecy in the Ancient Near East* (SBL WAW 12) documents the cross-cultural ANE distribution: the formula sits within a well-attested divine-encouragement-genre. See [al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula](#al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula) for the full cross-corpus treatment.

**The *anokhi Elohei Avraham avikha* formula** — *I am the Elohim of Avraham your father* — is the first canonical *anokhi Elohei X avikha* ancestral-god self-disclosure formula in the patriarchal narratives. The formula identifies the speaking deity through **ancestral-relational genealogy** rather than through self-naming or cosmological-predicate. The form is foundational for **Albrecht Alt**'s 1929 *Der Gott der Väter* (*The God of the Fathers*) reconstruction of the patriarchal-period ancestral-god religion: the pre-Mosaic religious-form in which each patriarchal-lineage worshipped the deity who had appeared to the lineage's founding patriarch. The cross-corpus deployments — Gen 28:13 (Ya'aqov's ladder); Gen 31:5, 31:42, 31:53; Gen 32:10; Gen 46:3; **Exod 3:6** (the burning bush — *Anokhi Elohei avikha Elohei Avraham Elohei Yitzchaq v-Elohei Ya'aqov*; the keystone deployment); Exod 3:13-16; 6:3 — make the formula one of the Pentateuch's foundational divine-name-disclosure clusters. The Alt 1929 reconstruction has been refined by **Cross** 1973 *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* ch. 1 (the Ugaritic-El-cult-identification), partly critiqued by **Van Seters** 1975 and **Thompson** 1974 (the patriarchal-narrative-historicity question), and held in modern-critical-consensus form by **Miller** 2000 and **Smith** 1990/2002. See [anokhi-elohei-X-avikha-ancestral-god-formula](#anokhi-elohei-X-avikha-ancestral-god-formula) for the full treatment.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֧בֶן שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וַיֶּט־שָׁ֖ם אָהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּכְרוּ־שָׁ֥ם עַבְדֵי־יִצְחָ֖ק בְּאֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And he built an altar there, and called on the name of YHWH, and pitched his tent there; and there Yitzchaq's servants dug a well.

paragraphs.commentary: Yitzchaq builds an altar and **calls on the name of YHWH** — the patriarchal altar-formula (see [qara-b-shem-yhwh](#qara-b-shem-yhwh)). The formula's recurrences mark altar-sites along the Avrahamic-and-Yitzchaq itineraries: Gen 12:8 (Avram between Beth-El and Ai); Gen 13:4 (Avram returning); Gen 21:33 (Avraham at Be'er Sheva after planting a tamarisk); Gen 26:25 (here — Yitzchaq at Be'er Sheva). Yitzchaq's altar at Be'er Sheva is the structural continuation of his father's altar at the same place — another instance of the chapter's **paternal-continuation** signature (see commentary on v 18).

paragraphs.text: וַאֲבִימֶ֕לֶךְ הָלַ֥ךְ אֵלָ֖יו מִגְּרָ֑ר וַאֲחֻזַּת֙ מֵֽרֵעֵ֔הוּ וּפִיכֹ֖ל שַׂר־צְבָאֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Then Avimelekh went to him from Gerar, and Achuzzat his friend, and Phicol the captain of his host.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Yitzchaq-Avimelekh covenant at Be'er Sheva (vv 26-31) is the structural doublet of the Avraham-Avimelekh covenant at Gen 21:22-32.** The two narratives share four structural features: (i) the same Philistine king (named *Avimelekh* in both, though the two are nominally distinct rulers separated by a generation); (ii) the same *Pichol sar tzva'o* military-commander epithet (Gen 21:22 / Gen 26:26); (iii) the same *Elohim/YHWH imkha* divine-presence-recognition formula (Gen 21:22 / Gen 26:28 — see commentary on v 28); (iv) the same *Be'er Sheva* covenant-site etiology (Gen 21:31 / Gen 26:33). The doublet relationship is documented in [wife-sister-type-scene](#wife-sister-type-scene) (which treats the wife-sister doublet across Gen 12, 20, 26) and is mirrored by the wife-sister doublet's parallel three-fold structure. The Gen 26 covenant differs in two key respects: (i) Avimelekh **initiates** the covenant-approach (where at Gen 21 Avraham hosts; here Avimelekh travels from Gerar to Be'er Sheva); (ii) the covenant resolves a **prior hostility** (Avimelekh's expulsion of Yitzchaq at v 16) rather than a neutral mutual-recognition (Gen 21:22-23's setting).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יִצְחָ֔ק מַדּ֖וּעַ בָּאתֶ֣ם אֵלָ֑י וְאַתֶּם֙ שְׂנֵאתֶ֣ם אֹתִ֔י וַתְּשַׁלְּח֖וּנִי מֵאִתְּכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq said to them, Why have you come to me, seeing you hate me, and have sent me away from you?

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ רָא֣וֹ רָאִינוּ֮ כִּֽי־הָיָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה ׀ עִמָּךְ֒ וַנֹּ֗אמֶר תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א אָלָ֛ה בֵּינוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְנִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And they said, We saw plainly that YHWH was with you; and we said, Let there now be an oath between us, between us and you, and let us cut a covenant with you,

paragraphs.commentary: *Ra'o ra'inu ki-hayah YHWH imakh* — *we saw plainly that YHWH was with you*. The verse is the structural near-doublet of Gen 21:22 (Avimelekh to Avraham: *Elohim imkha b-khol asher atah oseh* — *Elohim is with you in all that you do*; see [elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula](#elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula)). The doublet uses **YHWH** here where Gen 21:22 used **Elohim** — the divine-name shift is itself a documentary-source signal: the J-source (Yahwist) is generally associated with YHWH-use in patriarchal contexts, while the E-source (Elohist) is associated with Elohim-use; the Gen 21:22 / Gen 26:28 pair may reflect parallel J / E versions of the same narrative tradition. **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 343, 428 and **Friedman** *The Bible with Sources Revealed* 2003 read the doublet as source-critically distinct. The *external-recognition* register is foundational across both occurrences: a non-Israelite king explicitly identifies the patriarch as divinely-accompanied. See the [elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula](#elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula) entry for the full cross-corpus treatment; *appliesTo* now includes both GEN-WOH-21:22 and GEN-WOH-26:28.

paragraphs.text: אִם־תַּעֲשֵׂ֨ה עִמָּ֜נוּ רָעָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א נְגַֽעֲנ֔וּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֤ינוּ עִמְּךָ֙ רַק־ט֔וֹב וַנְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֖ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם אַתָּ֥ה עַתָּ֖ה בְּר֥וּךְ יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: That you will do us no harm, as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of YHWH.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃

i18n.en: And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ לְאָחִ֑יו וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֣ם יִצְחָ֔ק וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And they rose up early in the morning, and swore one to another; and Yitzchaq sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ עַל־אֹד֥וֹת הַבְּאֵ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑רוּ וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ מָצָ֥אנוּ מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass the same day, that Yitzchaq's servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had dug, and said to him, We have found water.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ שִׁבְעָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֤ן שֵׁם־הָעִיר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And he called it Shiv'ah; therefore the name of the city is Be'er Sheva to this day.

paragraphs.commentary: **The chapter's second Be'er Sheva etiology** — Yitzchaq's well-name *Shiv'ah* (שִׁבְעָה) — is the partial-sense doublet of the Gen 21:31 layered double-etymology (where Avraham's Be'er Sheva was named under both the seven-ewe-lambs *sheva* sense and the swearing *shava* sense; see [be-er-sheva-folk-etymology](#be-er-sheva-folk-etymology)). The Gen 26:33 etiology activates **only the *sheva*-as-oath sense** (the swearing-clause at v 31 *va-yishav'u ish l-achiv* — the verb *yishav'u*, niphal of *shava*) with no parallel to the seven-ewe-lambs object-arrangement of Gen 21. The two etiologies are deliberately partial-vs-layered: Gen 26:33 is single-sense (oath only); Gen 21:31 is double-sense (seven + oath). The doublet is part of the wider *wife-sister + Avimelekh + Be'er Sheva* triad-doublet across the Avraham and Yitzchaq cycles. The *appliesTo* of [be-er-sheva-folk-etymology](#be-er-sheva-folk-etymology) now includes GEN-WOH-26:23 and GEN-WOH-26:33.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֤י עֵשָׂו֙ בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־יְהוּדִ֔ית בַּת־בְּאֵרִ֖י הַֽחִתִּ֑י וְאֶת־בָּ֣שְׂמַ֔ת בַּת־אֵילֹ֖ן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And when Esav was forty years old, he took to wife Yehudit the daughter of Be'eri the Chitti, and Basemat the daughter of Elon the Chitti.

paragraphs.commentary: Esav at 40 takes two Chitti (Hittite) wives — Yehudit bat-Be'eri and Basemat bat-Elon. The wife-list is editorially-significant in three ways. **(i)** *Chitti* (Hittite) ethnonym — the patriarchal-narratives' *Chittim* are most plausibly the Canaanite-Hittite ethnonym rather than the Anatolian Late-Bronze-Age Hattusa-empire Hittites (the question is treated by the separate `bnei-het-hittites-canaanite-anatolian-question` entry, anchored at Gen 23's Hebron-Hittite trading-context; the Negev / Be'er Sheva locus of Gen 26:34 is consistent with the Canaanite-Hittite reading). **(ii)** **Wife-list inconsistency** — Esav's wife-list is given three different ways across Genesis: here (Yehudit bat-Be'eri, Basemat bat-Elon); Gen 28:9 (the Mahalat bat-Yishma'el addition after the Yitzchaq-blessing-stratagem); Gen 36:2-3 (the Esav-Edom-genealogy: Adah bat-Elon, Oholivamah bat-Anah, Basemat bat-Yishma'el). The three lists overlap partially but with different given-names and partly different ethnonyms (Chivvi vs Chitti). The rabbinic tradition (Gen Rab 65:2; Rashi at Gen 36:2) harmonizes by identifying the differently-named wives as the same persons; modern critical scholarship (Skinner *ICC* 1910 pp. 425-426; Westermann 1985 pp. 558-560; Friedman 2003) reads the lists as drawn from distinct documentary-sources. See [morat-ruach-bitterness-of-spirit-esau-hittite-wives](#morat-ruach-bitterness-of-spirit-esau-hittite-wives) for the full treatment. **(iii)** **Narrative-setup function** — the wife-introduction at v 34 and the *morat ruach* notice at v 35 together establish the conditions for Rivkah's stratagem in Gen 27 (the Yitzchaq-deathbed-blessing deception).

paragraphs.text: וַתִּהְיֶ֖יןָ מֹ֣רַת ר֑וּחַ לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּלְרִבְקָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And they were a bitterness of spirit to Yitzchaq and to Rivkah.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-tihyeinah morat ruach l-Yitzchaq u-l-Rivkah* — *and they were a bitterness of spirit to Yitzchaq and to Rivkah*. The construct *morat ruach* (מֹרַת רוּחַ) is a fixed-phrase combining *morah* (*bitterness, grief* — from the root *m-r-r*) with *ruach* (*spirit, breath, disposition*). The phrase is **virtually unique to Gen 26:35** in the HB. The choice of *ruach* (rather than *nefesh*) places the lexeme in the **dispositional-temperament** register — a persistent ongoing vexation — rather than the soul-level affliction register. **The verse is the chapter's narrative-pivot toward Gen 27.** Rivkah's complaint at Gen 27:46 — *qatzti b-chayyai mi-pnei b-not Chet* — *I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Chet* — is direct dialogue-quotation of this narrator's notice, and the wife-introduction-and-bitterness-notice together establish the motivation for Rivkah's stratagem to secure the Yitzchaq-deathbed-blessing for Ya'aqov. The chapter does not close with reconciliation; it closes with grievance — preparing the next chapter's deception.
